topic: Claude Opus 4.5 Is Not the Normal AI Agent Experience: A Developer's Perspective

key_points: Opus 4.5 is 'not the normal AI agent experience' — dramatically better than previous agents
Built a Windows image conversion utility in one shot with minimal intervention
Built a GIF recording utility similar to LICEcap with Opus 4.5
Opus 4.5 gets most things right on first try, self-iterates on errors
Used GitHub Copilot in VS Code with custom agent prompt, no fancy workflows needed
Claims AI coding agents can absolutely replace developers now
Top 0.01% Cursor user who switched to Claude Code 2.0 with Opus 4.5
RLHF on Opus 4.5 'completely changed the equation' — no longer need to review code line by line
5 pillars of agentic coding: context, planning, closing the loop, verifiability, debugging
Built a genetic algorithm simulator with interactive visualizations in 1 day without writing code
Uses Claude Code with Opus 4.5 for most tasks, Cursor with GPT 5.2 for UI perfection
Emphasizes planning leverage: good prompt saves 3 min of debugging per 1 min of planning
Counterpoint: AI handles writing code but leaves the hard work (investigation, context, validation)
Vibe coding has a ceiling — AI agent deleted 400 lines from a file when asked to add a test
AI is 'senior skill, junior trust' — writes well but needs careful review like a junior engineer
Reading AI-generated code is harder than writing your own — you lack the context
AI-assisted investigation is an underrated skill that takes practice
Burnout and shipping slop will eat whatever productivity gains AI gives you
AGENTS.md with compressed docs index achieved 100% pass rate vs 79% for skills with explicit instructions
Skills weren't triggered reliably — 56% of eval cases never invoked the skill
Passive context beats active retrieval: no decision point, consistent availability, no ordering issues
Compressed 8KB docs index embedded in AGENTS.md outperformed sophisticated skill-based retrieval
Key instruction: 'Prefer retrieval-led reasoning over pre-training-led reasoning'
Both Codex and Claude Code are already superhuman developers
Claude makes you feel like you're doing engineering work — many knobs to turn (CLAUDE.md, Skills, MCP)
Codex produces high-quality results out of the box with less need to be in the loop
Claude's Plan Mode is exceptional — asks many questions, interrupts itself to stay on track
Personal working style determines which tool is better — no wrong choice

stats.fact: Opus 4.5 achieved 100% pass rate on Vercel's Next.js 16 eval suite when docs were embedded in AGENTS.md
Skills were never invoked in 56% of eval cases without explicit instructions telling the agent to use them
Skills with explicit instructions achieved 79% pass rate vs 53% baseline (no docs)
A top 0.01% Cursor user switched to Claude Code 2.0 citing Opus 4.5 RLHF as the game-changer
Burke Holland built a Windows image conversion utility in one shot with Opus 4.5, calling it 'not the normal AI agent experience'
An AI agent deleted 400 lines from a 500-line file when asked to add a single test, demonstrating vibe coding's ceiling
Claude Code has a 200K context limit vs Codex (400K) and Gemini (1M)
The /insights command in Claude Code generates HTML reports analyzing usage patterns across all sessions

angles: Opus 4.5 represents a paradigm shift — the first model where you can test behaviors instead of reviewing code
The 'senior skill, junior trust' paradox: AI writes like a senior but needs junior-level oversight
Passive context (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) outperforms active retrieval (skills) — counterintuitive finding from Vercel
The tool you choose should match how you work: Claude Code for hands-on engineers, Codex for set-and-forget
Vibe coding has a ceiling — AI makes the easy part easier but the hard part (investigation, validation) harder
Planning leverage is the new multiplier: time spent planning is directly proportional to agent output quality
The 'closing the loop' principle: automation cost has collapsed, so automating repeated tasks is almost always worth it
